title: Brazilian jiu-jitsu: positions, sweeps, and submissions
note: BJJ is a hierarchy of positions: guard, half guard, side control, mount, and back control. Players improve position before attacking, then finish with chokes or joint locks, and a tap ends it. IBJJF scoring rewards control held for three seconds: takedown, sweep, and knee on belly 2, guard pass 3, mount and back control 4.

read.title: Position before submission
text: Brazilian jiu-jitsu is often called a game of human chess, and its board is a hierarchy of positions. On the bottom, the guard lets a player on the back control an opponent with the legs, whether locked in closed guard or working with feet and hooks in open guard. Half guard traps one leg. On top, side control pins the chest, mount sits astride the torso, and back control, with both heels hooked inside the thighs, is often the most dangerous of all.

The guiding rule is position before submission. A player on the bottom tries to sweep, reversing to the top, while the player on top tries to pass the guard and settle into side control or mount. Only from stable control do the finishing techniques, chokes and joint locks, become reliable. A tap, on the partner or the mat, ends the exchange.

IBJJF competition scoring mirrors this hierarchy. A position must be held for three seconds to score: takedowns, sweeps, and knee on belly earn 2 points, a guard pass 3, and mount or back control 4. Advantages break ties when points are equal.
